correctness.rationale: The graph H(3,3)=K3 square K3 square K3 has 27 vertices; independent faces are completely enumerated by recursive graph neighborhoods and independently by triples of compatible 3×3 partial-permutation layers (11,776 faces including the empty face). The prescribed complete pivot order yields 5,869 incidence pairs including empty, or 5,868 ordinary face-poset pairs plus one critical vertex and 38 critical four-faces. Reversal of every matched Hasse arrow leaves a directed graph on all 11,775 nonempty faces with 56,592 oriented covering relations; exhaustive topological sorting visits every vertex, so the matching is acyclic. Forman’s discrete Morse theorem supplies one 0-cell and 38 four-cells, with necessarily trivial attaching maps, proving the integral wedge equivalence. Independent mod-two chain ranks (0,26,244,1034,2044,1752,660,96,12) corroborate but do not replace the Morse proof. The supplied standalone Python program has been run and agrees with its observed-output file.

originality.rationale: The proved claim is the integral homotopy decomposition of the independence complex of the Cartesian threefold product K3 square K3 square K3. Search using H(3,3), ternary cube, Cartesian Hamming graph, three-dimensional rook, generalized chessboard and nonattacking rook terms found no earlier implication. The closest same-object 2016 primary study derives independence/separation numbers, not the simplicial homotopy type. The 2014 multiple-chessboard theorems concern two-dimensional boards; the 2023 categorical-product paper concerns a nonisomorphic graph. Distinct indexed complexes of the same 27-point set do not cover the result. Limited-access and unindexed sources remain residual risks, not evidence of absence.

value.rationale: The 27-vertex ternary Hamming three-cube is the natural minimum all-ternary three-coordinate Cartesian graph, a standard model for code selections and nonattacking rooks in three spatial directions. Its independence complex reaches dimension 8 but collapses homotopically to precisely 38 four-spheres. This exact integral homotopy classification is much stronger than the previously studied independence number or Betti ranks and offers a substantive benchmark for complexes of higher-dimensional rook graphs and Cartesian products; it is a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
